Anya: Quick thread to capture follow-ups after the console-RBAC RFC. We need a concrete invalidation strategy.
Ravi: yep, happy to sync.
Anya: core problem: perms change -> cached query results become stale. Options: short TTL, event-driven evict, include policy_rev in key, or cohorted keys + post-filter.
Becca: short TTL is simplest but kills hit rate. Event-driven ideal but we must guarantee delivery or reconcile.
Tom: including policy_rev in key is correct but causes cardinality explosion.
Ravi: cohorting looks promising: group tenants by permission cohorts (e.g., common role sets) and use cohort key; fallback to per-tenant filter for exceptions. Keeps cache size sane.
Anya: operationally: wire policy.changes kafka topic -> console-cache-invalidator consumer; tombstone keys on change, stagger evictions to avoid thundering-herd, and run daily reconcile job.
infra-bot: policy service: emits policy.changes v1. Recommend consumer group console-cache-invalidator.
Becca: metrics to add: console.cache.hit_rate_by_route, console.cache.evictions_per_min, batch.coalesce_rate, auth_invalidation.count.
Tom: streaming/live preview routes are latency-critical: prefer control-plane auth + short TTL. Analytics tiles can use cohorted cache + eventual filter.
Ravi: batching note: per-tenant filters reduce coalescing. We'll batch at prefix/model layer, then apply lightweight filter where possible.
Anya: rollout plan: 1) implement cohort keys + tombstone consumer (Ravi), 2) add headers X-Policy-Rev and X-Cache-Cohort (Becca), 3) canary hybrid mode for 10% orgs with reconcile enabled (Tom), 4) monitor metrics 48h and roll forward.
Becca: add canary triggers: drop in batch.coalesce_rate > 10% or evictions spike -> rollback.
Tom: I'll draft the runbook for disabling event invalidation and falling back to TTL.
Anya: decision: proceed hybrid (cohort + event invalidation + reconcile) with explicit route exceptions. I'll file follow-up RFC with checklist.
Ravi: will start consumer PR.
Becca: will add dashboards and alerts.
Tom: will update docs.
Anya: thanks all, closing thread.
